paragraphs: We are a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of therapeutics, starting with eye care. We launched XDEMVY® (lotilaner ophthalmic solution) 0.25%, formerly known as TP-03, for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis, in August 2023 after receiving U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") approval in July 2023. Demodex blepharitis is caused by the infestation of Demodex mites. Demodex blepharitis ("blephar" is a reference to eyelid and "itis" is a reference to inflammation) is a disease characterized by inflammation of the eyelid margin, redness and ocular irritation, including a specific type of eyelash dandruff called collarettes, which are pathognomonic for Demodex blepharitis. Poorly controlled and progressive Demodex blepharitis can lead to corneal damage over time and, in extreme cases, blindness. There may be as many as approximately 25 million people in the U.S. who suffer from Demodex blepharitis. XDEMVY is the first and only therapeutic approved by the FDA and we believe is the definitive standard of care for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis.

XDEMVY targets and eradicates the root cause of Demodex blepharitis - Demodex mite infestation. The active pharmaceutical ingredient ("API") of XDEMVY, lotilaner, paralyzes and eradicates mites and other parasites through the inhibition of parasite-specific gamma-aminobutyric acid-gated chloride ("GABA-Cl") channels with no GABA-Cl inhibition in humans.

To date, we have completed seven clinical trials that include a Phase 3 trial (the "Saturn-2 trial"), a Phase 2b/3 trial (the "Saturn-1 trial"), four Phase 2 trials, and a Phase 1 trial (the "Hyperion trial") for XDEMVY in Demodex blepharitis, all of which met their primary, secondary and/or certain exploratory endpoints, with the drug well tolerated throughout each trial. We have also completed clinical trials in Demodex blepharitis patients with Meibomian Gland Disease ("MGD"), including a Phase 2a clinical trial (the "Ersa trial") and a pilot clinical trial (the "Rhea trial") involving an XDEMVY vehicle.

We intend to further advance our pipeline with, e.g., the lotilaner API to address several diseases in human medicine, including eye care and infectious disease prevention. We are investigating the development of our product candidates to address targeted diseases with high unmet medical needs, which currently include TP-04, an investigational sterile aqueous gel formulation of lotilaner for the potential treatment of ocular rosacea, and TP-05, an investigational oral tablet formulation of lotilaner, for potential Lyme disease prophylaxis and community malaria reduction.

MGD is commonly characterized by functional and structural dysfunction of the meibomian glands within the eyelid margin, leading to blockage and/or thickened, decreased meibum production. If left untreated, MGD can lead to permanent changes to the tear film and progressive gland loss. Approximately 30-40 million Americans are impacted by MGD. Currently, there are no FDA-approved pharmacologic therapies for MGD patients. Demodex mites are key contributors to MGD in patients with Demodex blepharitis, causing eyelid inflammation and reduced meibomian gland function.

In December 2023, we announced positive topline results from the Ersa trial evaluating XDEMVY administered twice daily ("BID") or three times a day ("TID") for six weeks and twelve weeks for the treatment of MGD in patients with Demodex mites. XDEMVY demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements compared to baseline in two objective measures of the disease: the presence and quality of liquid secretion as measured by the Meibomian Gland Secretion Score; and the number of glands secreting normal or clear liquid. In November 2024, additional positive data was presented from the Ersa trial as well as data from the Rhea trial, at the American Academy of Optometry ("AAOpt") Annual Meeting 2024, and in April 2025 at the American Cataract and Refractive Surgery ("ASCRS") Annual Meeting 2025. The Rhea trial enrolled a similar patient population as the Ersa trial, and evaluated the same outcomes, with the same dosing regimens, except the Rhea trial participants received XDEMVY vehicle. Both the Ersa and Rhea trials also assessed patient reported outcomes for some of the most commonly reported patient symptoms in Demodex blepharitis and MGD, namely fluctuating vision, itching, redness, and burning.

The presentations, which combined the Ersa and Rhea trials data in a pooled analysis, demonstrated that XDEMVY provided statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements of the meibomian glands from baseline and when compared to vehicle, including at least three times more glands secreting normal or clear liquid in patients treated with XDEMVY compared to vehicle at day 43. These improvements were shown across three objective measures of MGD: (i) the presence and quality of liquid secretion as measured by the Meibomian Gland Secretion Score; (ii) the number of glands

secreting normal or clear liquid; and (iii) the number of glands yielding any liquid. Improvements were also demonstrated across certain patient reported outcomes, including fluctuating vision, itching and redness. Further, XDEMVY demonstrated statistically significant rates of collarette cure and lid margin erythema cure that are consistent with previous XDEMVY studies. No statistically significant differences were observed between the BID and TID treatment arms in both the Ersa and Rhea trials, respectively, and XDEMVY and the XDEMVY vehicle were well tolerated. Given the positive results of these trials, plus the FDA's feedback that these patients are already covered under XDEMVY's label for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis, our medical affairs and sales teams are sharing some of this data with eye care professionals ("ECPs").

We are exploring the therapeutic potential of TP-04 as an investigational sterile aqueous gel formulation of lotilaner, for the treatment of ocular rosacea, a chronic eye disease characterized by prominent and visible blood vessels, or telangiectasia, as well as redness, flushing and inflammation of the eyelid margin and surrounding peri-ocular skin. Ocular rosacea is a highly prevalent disease, with approximately 15-18 million Americans impacted by ocular rosacea and there are currently no FDA-approved therapeutics to treat this disease. One of the potential root causes of ocular rosacea, similar to Demodex blepharitis, is believed to be Demodex mites. As shown below, Figure 1 illustrates visible blood vessels known as telangiectasia, and Figure 2 illustrates eyelid inflammation and redness.

TP-04 is designed to eradicate Demodex mites. In March 2023, we announced positive topline results from the Phase 1 Galatea trial (the "Galatea Phase 1 trial") and initiated a Phase 2a trial (the "Galatea trial") for the potential treatment of papulopustular rosacea. The Galatea trial was a multicenter, randomized, vehicle-controlled trial evaluating the safety, tolerability and efficacy of TP-04. In February 2024, we announced positive topline results from the Galatea trial which demonstrated statistically significant improvements (p<0.05) in inflammatory lesions and Investigator's Global Assessment ("IGA") score (change in baseline and success rate) were observed compared to vehicle at Week 12. TP-04 was generally well tolerated.

After review of this data with the FDA and key opinion leaders ("KOLs"), we decided to pursue development of TP-04 for the potential treatment for ocular rosacea. In December 2025, we initiated a Phase 2 trial for the potential treatment of ocular rosacea with topline results expected in the first half of 2027.

We are exploring the therapeutic potential of TP-05 as a systemic prophylactic for Lyme disease designed to eradicate the tick before it can transmit the Borrelia bacteria that causes Lyme disease. There are approximately 80 million people in the U.S. at risk of Lyme disease exposure with nearly 30 million of which are moderate to high risk. Further, there are approximately 400,000 reported cases of Lyme disease in the U.S. each year, but it is believed that the actual number of cases could be much higher.

Lyme disease can potentially cause severe, often debilitating symptoms with permanent and irreversible damage. The disease can result in inflammation, nerve, joint and muscle pain or swelling, numbness, shortness of breath and, in severe cases, neurological complications such as facial palsy, vision issues and meningitis, including severe headaches and neck stiffness. Lyme disease can often go undetected and untreated because the ticks are not always noticed before they transmit the disease. People who are in high-risk areas and/or spend extended amounts of time outdoors in wooded, grassy areas are at higher risk of contracting the infection. Data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention ("CDC") show that the risk of Lyme disease is spreading to new geographic areas, resulting in a significant need for prophylactic solutions.

Currently, there are no FDA-approved pharmacological prophylactic options for Lyme disease. We believe TP-05 is currently the only on-demand, oral tablet in development that targets ticks and potentially prevents Lyme disease transmission. It is designed to rapidly and durably provide systemic levels of lotilaner potentially sufficient to kill infected ticks attached to the human body through selective targeting of parasite-specific GABA-CI channels, before they can transmit the Borrelia bacteria.

headings: Risks Related to our Business and Operations

We expect to expand our development, regulatory, operational, sales, marketing, and distribution capabilities and, as a result, we may encounter difficulties in managing our growth, which could disrupt our operations.
Our future success depends on our ability to retain key employees, consultants and advisors and to attract, retain and motivate qualified personnel.

Product liability lawsuits against us could cause us to incur substantial liabilities, could divert our resources and could limit or delay our commercialization of XDEMVY or any product candidates that we may develop.
Unfavorable global and geopolitical economic conditions could adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.
Risks Related to Development and Commercialization

We are heavily dependent on the continued successful commercialization of XDEMVY and the successful development, regulatory approvals, and commercialization of our current and future product candidates.
paragraphs: Investing in our common stock is speculative and involves a high degree of risk. Before investing in our common stock, you should consider carefully the risks described below, together with the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our financial statements and the related notes appearing at the end of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations and future growth prospects could be materially and adversely affected. In these circumstances, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. The risks described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks that we are unaware of, or that we currently believe are not material, may also become important factors that affect us. This Annual Report on Form 10-K also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of a number of factors, including the risks described below. See "Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements."

We are a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company with a limited operating history and a single product approved for commercial sale. While we have generated revenue from the launch of XDEMVY® (lotilaner ophthalmic solution) 0.25%, we have continued to incur losses and negative cash flows from operations since our inception and anticipate that we could continue to incur significant expenses and potential losses in the future.

We have one product, XDEMVY®, formerly known as TP-03, which obtained Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") approval for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis in the U.S. in July 2023. We have incurred net losses each year since our Company's formation in 2016. We have funded our operations primarily from the sale and issuance of redeemable convertible preferred stock, convertible promissory notes and the sale of our common stock in our IPO, subsequent Follow-On Public Offerings, and under our 2023 ATM Prospectus, as well as proceeds from product sales, net, our China Out-License and draws from our Credit Facilities (as defined below). For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, our net losses were $66.4 million, $115.6 million, and $135.9 million, respectively. As of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, we had an accumulated deficit of $426.6 million and $360.2 million, respectively. Additionally, the net losses we incur may fluctuate significantly from quarter to quarter such that a period-to-period comparison of our results of operations may not be a good indicator of our future performance. The size of potential future net losses will depend, in part, on the rate of future growth of our expenses and our ability to generate revenue. We initiated sales and marketing activities to commercialize XDEMVY in August 2023. We could potentially incur operating losses in the future until our revenue from product sales from XDEMVY and any other approved products exceeds expenses. We may never achieve profitability and, even if we do, we may not be able to sustain or increase our profitability. Our prior losses, combined with potential future losses, have had and could continue to have an adverse effect on our accumulated deficit and working capital.
We could continue incurring significant expenses and potential operating losses in the future. We expect that our expenses will increase substantially as we:
•continue to commercialize XDEMVY and any other products for which we may obtain marketing approval;

•enhance our product development and planned future commercialization efforts of our product candidates, including through hiring additional clinical, regulatory, quality control and scientific personnel;

paragraphs: 本公司為一家商業階段的生物製藥公司，專注於開發與商業化治療藥物，起點為眼疾治療。我們於2023年8月推出XDEMVY®（lotilaner眼用溶液）0.25%，先前稱為TP-03，用於治療Demodex結膜炎，此藥物於2023年7月獲得美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准。Demodex結膜炎是由Demodex蠕蟲感染所引起。Demodex結膜炎（"blephar"為眼瞼的參考，"itis"為發炎的參考）是一種以眼瞼邊緣發炎、紅腫及眼睛刺激為特徵的疾病，包括一種特定類型的眼睫毛脫屑稱為collarettes，此為Demodex結膜炎的特徵性表現。若Demodex結膜炎控制不佳且持續惡化，可能會導致角膜損傷，極端情況下甚至導致失明。美國可能有約25百萬人受Demodex結膜炎所苦。XDEMVY為美國食品藥物管理局核准的首個且唯一治療Demodex結膜炎的藥物，我們相信這是治療Demodex結膜炎的確診標準照護。
XDEMVY針對並消除Demodex結膜炎的根本原因－Demodex蠕蟲感染。XDEMVY的活性藥物成分（"API"）lotilaner，透過抑制寄生蟲特有的γ-氨基丁酸 gated 氯離子（"GABA-Cl"）通道，使蠕蟲麻痹並消除，而對人類的GABA-Cl通道則無抑制作用。

截至目前為止，我們已完成七項臨牀試驗，包括一項第三期試驗（"Saturn-2試驗"）、一項第二期/第三期試驗（"Saturn-1試驗"）、四項第二期試驗，以及一項第一期試驗（"Hyperion試驗"），用於XDEMVY在Demodex結膜炎的治療，所有試驗均達成其主要、次要及/或某些探索性終點，且藥物在各試驗中均被良好耐受。我們也已完成針對Demodex結膜炎患者伴隨Meibomian腺體疾病（"MGD"）的臨牀試驗，包括一項第二期a臨牀試驗（"Ersa試驗"）及一項試驗性臨牀試驗（"Rhea試驗"），其中包含XDEMVY的載體。
我們計畫進一步推進我們的產品線，例如使用lotilaner API來解決人類醫學中多種疾病，包括眼疾及感染預防。我們正在研究開發我們的產品候選藥物，以針對具有高未滿足醫療需求的特定疾病，目前包括TP-04，一種lotilaner的無菌水凝膠製劑，用於潛在治療眼 rosacea，以及TP-05，一種lotilaner的口服片劑，用於潛在的萊姆病預防及社區瘧疾減少。
MGD通常特徵為眼瞼邊緣內的Meibomian腺體功能性及結構性功能異常，導致阻塞及/或Meibum產生減少、變厚。若未治療，MGD可能會導致淚液層的永久性改變及腺體逐漸喪失。約有30-40百萬美國人受MGD所影響。目前尚無FDA核准的藥物治療MGD患者。Demodex蠕蟲是MGD患者中Demodex結膜炎的關鍵因素，導致眼瞼發炎及Meibomian腺體功能下降。

我們於2023年12月宣佈，從評估XDEMVY每日兩次（"BID"）或每日三次（"TID"）治療MGD患者的Ersa試驗中，獲得正面的初步結果，治療時間為六週及十二週。XDEMVY在兩項疾病客觀指標上顯示統計顯著且臨牀意義重大的改善，與基準值相比：Meibomian腺體分泌評分所測得的液體存在與品質；以及分泌正常或清澈液體的腺體數量。2024年11月，Ersa試驗的更多正面數據以及Rhea試驗的數據，在美國視光學會（"AAOpt"）年度會議2024中發表，並在2025年4月的美國白內障與屈光手術協會（"ASCRS"）年度會議2025中發表。Rhea試驗納入的患者羣與Ersa試驗相似，評估相同的結果，並使用相同的給藥方案，除了Rhea試驗參與者接受XDEMVY載體。Ersa與Rhea試驗也評估了Demodex結膜炎與MGD患者最常報告的症狀，如視力波動、癢、紅腫及灼熱感的患者報告結果。

這些報告結合了Ersa與Rhea試驗的數據，進行整體分析，顯示XDEMVY從基準值及與載體比較時，提供了統計顯著且臨牀意義重大的Meibomian腺體改善，包括接受XDEMVY治療的患者在第43天時，至少有三倍以上的腺體分泌正常或清澈液體，與載體相比。這些改善在三個MGD的客觀指標中顯示：(i) Meibomian腺體分泌評分所測得的液體存在與品質；(ii) 分泌正常或清澈液體的腺體數量；以及(iii) 產生任何液體的腺體數量。改善也顯示在某些患者報告結果中，包括視力波動、癢及紅腫。此外，XDEMVY顯示統計顯著的collarette治癒率及眼瞼邊緣紅腫治癒率，與先前XDEMVY研究結果一致。在Ersa與Rhea試驗中，BID與TID治療組間未觀察到統計顯著的差異，且XDEMVY與XDEMVY載體均被良好耐受。考慮到這些試驗的正面結果，加上FDA的反饋指出這些患者已涵蓋在XDEMVY用於治療Demodex結膜炎的標籤中，我們的醫療事務與銷售團隊正與眼科專業人員（"ECPs"）分享部分數據。

Improvements were also demonstrated across certain patient reported outcomes, including fluctuating vision, itching and redness. Further, XDEMVY demonstrated statistically significant rates of collarette cure and lid margin erythema cure that are consistent with previous XDEMVY studies. No statistically significant differences were observed between the BID and TID treatment arms in both the Ersa and Rhea trials, respectively, and XDEMVY and the XDEMVY vehicle were well tolerated. Given the positive results of these trials, plus the FDA's feedback that these patients are already covered under XDEMVY's label for the treatment of Demodex blepharitis, our medical affairs and sales teams are sharing some of this data with eye care professionals ("ECPs").

本公司正在探討 TP-04 的治療潛力，作為一種 Investigational 無菌水凝膠製劑的 lotilaner，用以治療慢性眼疾_ocular rosacea_，其特徵為明顯且可見的血管擴張，即 telangiectasia，以及眼瞼邊緣與周圍眼周皮膚的紅腫、發熱與發炎。_Ocular rosacea_ 是一種高度普遍的疾病，約有 15-18 百萬美國人受其影響，目前尚無美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准的治療方式。_Ocular rosacea_ 的潛在根本原因之一，與 Demodex blepharitis 相似，被認為是 Demodex 蟎蟲。如圖所示，圖 1 顯示可見的血管擴張，即 telangiectasia，圖 2 顯示眼瞼發炎與紅腫。

TP-04 設計用以消除 Demodex 蟎蟲。2023 年 3 月，本公司宣佈 Phase 1 Galatea 試驗（"Galatea Phase 1 試驗"）的初步結果為正面，並啟動 Phase 2a 試驗（"Galatea 試驗"）用以潛在治療丘疹性痤瘡。Galatea 試驗為多中心、隨機、安慰劑對照試驗，評估 TP-04 的安全性、耐受性與療效。2024 年 2 月，本公司宣佈 Galatea 試驗的初步結果為正面，顯示在第 12 週時，與安慰劑相比，發炎性病竈與 Investigator's Global Assessment（"IGA"）評分（基線變動與成功率）觀察到統計學顯著改善（p<0.05）。TP-04 通常耐受性良好。
在與美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）及權威意見領袖（"KOLs"）審閱此資料後，本公司決定推動 TP-04 用以潛在治療_ocular rosacea_。2025 年 12 月，本公司啟動 Phase 2 試驗用以潛在治療_ocular rosacea_，預計 2027 年第一季公佈初步結果。
本公司正在探討 TP-05 的治療潛力，作為一種系統性預防藥物，用以預防 Lyme 病毒的傳播，設計用以在蜱蟲傳播 Borrelia 病毒之前殺死蜱蟲。美國約有 80 百萬人有 Lyme 病毒感染風險，其中約有 30 百萬人屬於中高風險。進一步而言，美國每年約有 400,000 個 Lyme 病毒病例被報導，但實際病例數可能遠高於此。

Lyme 病毒可能導致嚴重、常見且使人無法工作的症狀，並造成永久且不可逆的傷害。此疾病可能導致發炎、神經、關節與肌肉疼痛或腫脹、麻木、呼吸困難，嚴重情況下甚至會導致神經系統併發症，例如面部麻痺、視力問題與腦膜炎，包括嚴重頭痛與頸部僵硬。Lyme 病毒常因蜱蟲未被察覺而未被診斷與治療。居住在高風險地區或長時間在林地、草地等戶外活動的人，感染風險較高。根據美國疾病管制與預防中心（"CDC"）的資料，Lyme 病毒的風險正在擴展至新的地理區域，導致對預防性解決方案有顯著需求。
目前尚無美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准的藥物預防性選項用以治療 Lyme 病毒。本公司認為 TP-05 是目前唯一正在開發的、可按需使用的口服藥片，目標為蜱蟲，並可能預防 Lyme 病毒的傳播。其設計用以快速且持續提供系統性 lotilaner 濃度，可能足夠殺死附著在人體上的受感染蜱蟲，透過選擇性針對寄生蟲特定 GABA-CI 頻道，使其在傳播 Borrelia 病毒之前被清除。

paragraphs: 下列對我們財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析，應與我們的「選取財務資料」及財務報表與相關附註說明一併閱讀，這些資料包含於本年度10-K表報告的其他部分。除了歷史財務資訊外，下列討論與分析包含許多前瞻性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險、不確定性與假設。我們實際的結果與特定事件的時間點可能與這些前瞻性陳述所預期的有重大差異，這是因為許多因素，包括但不限於於「風險因素」節中討論的內容及其他本年度10-K表報告中提及的內容。請參閱本年度10-K表報告中標題為「關於前瞻性陳述的說明」的節次。

我們是一家商業階段的生物製藥公司，專注於開發與商業化治療藥物，起點為眼疾治療。我們於2023年8月推出XDEMVY®（lotilaner眼用溶液）0.25%，先前稱為TP-03，用於治療Demodex結膜炎，此藥物於2023年7月獲得美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准。Demodex結膜炎是由Demodex蠕形蟎感染所引起。Demodex結膜炎（"blephar"是指眼瞼，"itis"是指發炎）是一種眼科眼瞼邊緣疾病，特徵為眼瞼邊緣發炎、紅腫與眼睛刺激，包括一種特定類型的眼睫毛脫屑稱為collarettes，這為Demodex結膜炎的特徵性表現。若Demodex結膜炎控制不佳且持續惡化，可能會導致角膜損傷，極端情況下甚至導致失明。美國可能有約25百萬人罹患Demodex結膜炎。XDEMVY是美國食品藥物管理局核准的第一個且唯一治療Demodex結膜炎的藥物，我們相信它是治療Demodex結膜炎的確診標準照護。
XDEMVY針對並消除Demodex結膜炎的根本原因—Demodex蠕形蟎感染。XDEMVY的活性藥物成分（"API"）lotilaner，透過抑制蠕形蟎特異性γ-氨基丁酸門控氯離子（"GABA-Cl"）通道，使蠕形蟎及其他寄生蟲癱瘓並被清除，而對人類的GABA-Cl通道則無抑制作用。

截至目前為止，我們已完成七項臨牀試驗，包括一項Phase 3 Saturn-2試驗、一項Phase 2b/3 Saturn-1試驗、四項Phase 2試驗，以及一項Phase 1試驗，用於XDEMVY在Demodex結膜炎的應用，所有試驗均達成其主要、次要及/或某些探索性終點，且藥物在各試驗中均被良好耐受。我們也已完成針對患有Meibomian腺體疾病（"MGD"）的Demodex結膜炎患者的臨牀試驗，包括一項Phase 2a臨牀試驗（"Ersa試驗"），以及一項小型臨牀試驗（"Rhea試驗"）涉及XDEMVY的載體。
我們有意進一步推進我們的產品線，例如使用lotilaner API來針對人類醫學中的多種疾病，包括眼疾治療與感染疾病預防。我們正在研究開發我們的產品候選藥物以針對具有高未滿足醫療需求的特定疾病，目前包括TP-04，一種lotilaner的實驗性無菌水凝膠製劑，用於潛在治療眼 rosacea，以及TP-05，一種lotilaner的實驗性口服片劑，用於潛在的萊姆病預防與社區瘧疾減少。
•XDEMVY是銷售最好的處方眼藥水之一。
◦淨產品銷售額為 151.7 百萬美元及 451.4 百萬美元，分別為 2025 年第四季及全年之數額。
◦第四季及2025年全年分別交付約130,000瓶與400,000瓶至患者手中。
◦維持超過 90% 的商業、醫療保險及醫療補助計畫覆蓋人數，並在 2025 年第四季及全年分別認列約 44% 與 45% 的毛利至淨利折扣。
•直接對消費者（"DTC"）在串流平台及電視網的行銷活動，於 2025 年產生正向的投資回報，且持續成長。
◦對 Demodex 眼瞼炎的無提示認知度現為約 25%，相較於活動開始時受訪患者僅為 2%。
•我們持續執行我們的創類別策略，推進強勁的產品管線。
•透過任命 David E.I. Pyott，一位知名生物製藥領導者及 Allergan Inc. 前執行長與董事長，強化我們的領導地位至董事會。
◦Mr. Pyott 於 2026 年 2 月加入我們的董事會，帶來數十年的全球領導經驗，涵蓋創新研發、產品開發與商業執行。他對於將 Allergan 從一個約 1 十億美元營收的眼科專注業務，轉型為全球專利藥品與醫療器材領導者，營收超過 7 十億美元，發揮關鍵作用。

headings: 與我們業務及營運相關的風險
我們預期將擴展我們的開發、法規、營運、銷售、行銷及分銷能力，因此我們可能在管理成長時遇到困難，這可能會干擾我們的營運。
我們未來的成功取決於我們保留關鍵員工、顧問及顧問的能力，以及吸引、保留並激勵合格人才的能力。
針對我們的產品責任訴訟可能會導致我們產生重大負債，可能會分散我們的資源，並可能限制或延遲我們XDEMVY或任何我們可能開發的產品候選品的商業化。
不利的全球及地緣政治經濟條件可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果產生負面影響。
與開發及商業化相關的風險
我們高度依賴XDEMVY的持續成功商業化，以及我們現有及未來產品候選品的開發、法規批准及商業化成功。
paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股屬於高度風險的投機行為。在投資本公司普通股前，您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，並配合本年度10-K表報表中其他資訊，包括財務報表及相關附註。若下列任何風險發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果及未來成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。下列所描述的風險並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險，可能是本公司未察覺，或目前認為不具重大影響，但未來可能成為影響本公司的重要因素。本年度10-K表報表中亦包含前瞻性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險與不確定性。本公司實際結果可能與前瞻性陳述中預期的結果有重大差異，原因可能是多種因素，包括下列所描述的風險。請參閱「關於前瞻性陳述的說明」。
本公司為一家商業階段的生技藥品公司，營運歷史有限，且僅有一項產品已核准上市販售。雖然本公司已從XDEMVY®（lotilaner眼用溶液0.25%）的上市銷售中獲取收入，但自本公司成立以來，持續產生虧損與營運現金流為負，預期未來可能持續產生重大支出與潛在虧損。

本公司僅有一項產品XDEMVY®，先前稱為TP-03，已獲得美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）核准，用於治療美國的Demodex blepharitis（蠕形蟎性結膜炎），時間為2023年7月。自本公司成立以來，每年均產生淨虧損。本公司主要透過發行可轉換優先股、可轉換貸款憑證及在IPO（首次公開發行股票）、隨後的公開發行及2023年ATM發行計畫下銷售普通股，以及產品銷售淨收入、中國授權銷售及信貸融資（如後文所定義）的資金來支應營運。截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日，本公司淨虧損分別為66.4百萬美元、115.6百萬美元及135.9百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日，本公司累計虧損分別為426.6百萬美元及360.2百萬美元。此外，本公司所產生的淨虧損可能在每季之間大幅波動，使得對本公司營運成果的期間比較可能無法作為未來表現的可靠指標。未來潛在淨虧損的規模，部分取決於未來支出成長的速度及本公司產生收入的能力。本公司於2023年8月開始進行XDEMVY的銷售與行銷活動，以實現其商業化。本公司未來可能持續產生營運虧損，直到XDEMVY及其他核准產品的銷售收入超過支出為止。本公司可能永遠無法實現盈利，即使實現盈利，也可能無法維持或提高盈利水平。本公司過去的虧損，加上未來可能的虧損，已對本公司累計虧損及營運資金產生並可能持續產生負面影響。
本公司未來可能持續產生重大支出與潛在營運虧損。本公司預期支出將因以下原因大幅增加：
•持續商業化XDEMVY及任何其他已獲得行銷核准的產品；
•加強產品開發與未來商業化計畫的相關努力，包括透過聘僱更多臨牀、法規、品質控制及科學人員。
